sections.h2: Who to call about a Hart County tax bill
sections.html:
Hart County runs its tax work from Main Street in Munfordville. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assigns each parcel a value, the sheriff takes the money, and the clerk records deeds and inherits bills that nobody paid.

  • PVA: P.O. Box 566, Munfordville, KY 42765, phone (270) 524-2321, weekday hours of 8 until 4.
  • Sheriff: 100 Main Street, phone (270) 524-2341. The sheriff's page directs owners to hartcountysheriffky.com for online payment.
  • Clerk: 200 Main Street, phone (270) 524-2751, open weekdays 8 until 4 and Saturday mornings from 9 to noon.

State law names the sheriff as collector of state, county, school and special district taxes (KRS 134.119). The sheriff may take part payments, and a relative, tenant or lender can pay on the owner's behalf.

Hart County is cave country in south central Kentucky. Munfordville is the seat and Horse Cave is the biggest city. The population was 20,117 in the July 2025 estimate, up 4.3 percent from April 2020, and the county has 9,192 housing units. Owners occupy 72.4 percent of homes, and the middle owner home value is $146,000. Middle owner cost is $1,140 a month with a mortgage, middle gross rent is $693, and middle household income is $52,285. Permits for 272 new buildings were issued in 2025.

A fire at the courthouse in January 1928 consumed some county records. A seller of an older farm who finds holes in the title paperwork can ask the clerk what survives for that parcel. Hart County keeps Central time, so confirm which clock your closing office follows.

Taxes are due by the last day of the assessment year, and KRS 134.015 adds a reward for early payers and a surcharge for late ones.

Hart County payment windows
Payment dateAmount due
On or before Nov. 1Bill reduced 2 percent when paid whole
Nov. 2 through Dec. 31Face value
JanuaryFace value plus 5 percent
LaterFace value plus 10 percent

The PVA can tell you who is listed as owner on January 1, since that date controls the name printed on the bill. Someone who closes in spring will probably see the first bill arrive addressed to the seller, so decide at the table who covers it.

Talk to the PVA, and if that fails, petition the county board of assessment appeals. The process sits in KRS 133.120, which the 2026 General Assembly rewrote.

  1. Ask for a conference with the PVA or a deputy. Phone conferences are allowed on request.
  2. Still unhappy? Put the appeal in writing and deliver it to the clerk's office by the workday after inspection closes. Cover three points: your objections, the parcel's identity, and your own valuation.
  3. Show up at the hearing with documents: listings, comparable sales, insurance records, building cost or loan papers. A petition with no facts behind it is denied.

The board meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends (KRS 133.030) and visits the property when asked. Meanwhile you owe tax on the number you claimed, and the board's final number may bring a bill for the difference.

The exemption is for a person over 65 or totally disabled who lives in the house. The Revenue Department's deduction for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100. File with the Hart County PVA, and report a sale so the deduction ends at the old address and can be claimed again at your next home.

Back taxes ride along with the land. A lien for delinquency under KRS 134.420 stays attached after a sale, which is why title searches find it.

Ask the sheriff for a payoff before listing. Once claims pass to the clerk, KRS 134.119 piles a collection fee on top (ten percent of the tax plus ten percent of the penalty), and an investor may buy the certificate and add interest. Closing offers the cleanest fix: the title company deducts the payoff from your proceeds. A cash buyer who takes the house as is can close on a short timeline, which leaves less time for charges to build.

The seller pays a Kentucky levy of $0.50 on each $500 of price, or part of $500. The clerk takes the money first and records afterward (KRS 142.050). The clerk's office on Main Street in Munfordville holds the county's land records, so call (270) 524-2751 for the current recording charge.

The sheriff is the collector, and the online payment page at hartcountysheriffky.com is the quickest route. You can also go to the office at 100 Main Street, or call (270) 524-2341 to ask how the office handles mailed checks. Because the sheriff may take part payments, an owner who is short of cash can chip away at a bill, but the 2 percent discount applies only when the bill is paid whole on or before November 1.

Anyone can pay on the owner's behalf. A relative, a tenant or a lender can send the money, which helps if you are selling from out of town or an heir is settling an estate. Keep the receipt, because the title company may ask for proof that the year is paid.

sections.h2: What the PVA does before and after a sale
sections.html:
The PVA's job ends at valuation, but its records drive everything else. It keeps the name of the January 1 owner, the assessed value and the exemption file. After you sell, the office needs to learn about the transfer so the old homestead deduction stops and the new owner's bill goes to the right address. The clerk records the deed, and the PVA picks up the change from that record, so the sooner the deed is recorded, the sooner the files match.

If you disagree with a value while a sale is pending, remember the appeal route is slow. The board meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends, so an appeal will rarely finish before a quick closing. Plan to settle the bill as it stands and sort out any difference with the buyer in the contract.

A quick sequence keeps tax questions from slowing the sale. Check the bill with the sheriff and confirm whether this year is paid. Ask the PVA who is listed as owner and whether your homestead deduction is on file. Ask the clerk what recorded papers exist for the parcel, especially on an older farm. Decide with the buyer who will pay the current bill, and put that on the settlement statement.

If you are paying near the November 1 cutoff, a closing that finishes before then lets the full-payment discount still apply to the bill. A closing after January means the 5 percent or 10 percent add-on may already be on it.

faqs.q: Which office mails the Hart County tax bill?
faqs.a: The sheriff, at (270) 524-2341. The PVA supplies the value, and the clerk picks up claims the sheriff could not collect.

faqs.q: How large is the homestead deduction for Hart County owners?
faqs.a: $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It goes to owners over 65 or totally disabled who apply with the PVA at (270) 524-2321.

faqs.q: Does Hart County reward early payment?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the whole bill by November 1 cuts it 2 percent. Missing December 31 adds 5 percent through January and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: Do I stop paying while my Hart County appeal is pending?
faqs.a: No. Meanwhile you owe tax on the figure you claimed, and a higher ruling brings a second bill with interest.

faqs.q: Can a Hart County house with back taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, with the debt settled at closing. Obtain a payoff from the sheriff and have the title company send it from your proceeds.
